metadata.note: Command teardown of ./art final — the dispatcher case at art:111-116 that forwards to python3 runtime/scripts/compile.py, defaulting --height 2160 when unset. compile.py is the assembler AND the review-cut compiler; --review draws beat labels and stays beside the reel, no --review writes a verified master to --out. final_preflight (paperwork triad + beat_lint + gate_shape) runs before rendering; final_frame_check (Gate V) runs against the candidate encode; approvals are re-checked and input SHA-256s re-hashed after the encode so a mid-render edit invalidates the cut. Successful finals ship with a sibling verified.json receipt (output SHA-256, input SHA-256, duration, timestamp). Slates and pending approvals block the master unconditionally; --allow-slates is review-only. All demo output in demo/RUN-LOG.txt is verbatim from this workstation against /tmp/claude-501/art-final-demo/ and /tmp/claude-501/art-final-slate-demo/. Playlist adaptation for @HumanitariansAI: composer folder chip reads @HumanitariansAI; outro card is the locked ClaudeTitleOutro with hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK.md — flagged for the human reviewer before publication. No paid API, no upload, no network calls. episode.source_sha256 5c4110bae43e20554516f1eabb31aff2a2f84e2f32d4c46e9b91fa51f03c4b43. props.command: Compile this reel to a verified 4K master. Refuse on thin paperwork or an unfilled slate. If the new export fails any check, keep the last good file in place. Do not print ready unless the file on disk really is.
output: gate F (paperwork) → gate LINT → gate SHAPE → render slots → encode candidate
gate V (frame-level QC) on the candidate mp4, then re-check approvals + input hashes
atomic replace of the master; write sibling verified.json (SHA-256, inputs, duration)

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — Beat 2 BLUF, written by the hesitant writer. Correction is the reel's actual misconception.
beats.narration_text: Watch the writer walk this back. Art final does not render once. It gates the paperwork, renders, and then re-verifies the output it just wrote. Two lines of defence, one written next to the other on the receipt.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — the dispatcher case at art:111-116. Two-branch height default, forwards to compile.py.
beats.narration_text: The dispatcher is one case in the art file. It matches the exact string final, checks whether you already passed a --height, and forwards everything to compile.py. If you did not name a height, it hardcodes 2160 — the native 4K master. There are no aliases. Every rule the command enforces lives inside compile.py.

show.event: code card fades in; title bar reads 'art'
spark line settles under the card

props.title: art:111-116 — one branch, two paths
props.code:
# From the top-level art dispatcher (bash):
case "$cmd" in
  # ...
  final)
    case " $* " in
      *" --height "*|*" --height="*)
        exec python3 "$ART_HOME/runtime/scripts/compile.py" "$@" ;;
      *)
        exec python3 "$ART_HOME/runtime/scripts/compile.py" "$@" --height 2160 ;;
    esac
    ;;
  # ...
esac

# The wrapper always: (1) resolves ART_HOME from art's own path,
# (2) execs python3 on compile.py, (3) forwards "$@" untouched,
# (4) if no --height was named, appends --height 2160 for 4K.
props.sparkLine: One case. No aliases. --height defaults to 4K.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — compile.py argparse surface. --review vs no-review is the whole two-verb split.
beats.narration_text: Compile.py's argparse surface is small on purpose. A reel folder. Optional --review, which is the reason art run and art final are the same script — the review path draws beat labels and stays beside the reel. Then --fps, --height, --audio, --force, --allow-slates, and --out. --allow-slates is review-only; a final refuses slates unconditionally. --out picks the destination — a local folder, a mounted drive, anywhere.

show.event: code card in; title reads 'compile.py — the small surface'
final vs review distinction card lands

props.title: compile.py — the small surface
props.code:
# runtime/scripts/compile.py — argparse surface
ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("folder", type=Path)
ap.add_argument("--review",       action="store_true")
ap.add_argument("--fps",    type=int, default=24)
ap.add_argument("--height", type=int, default=720)   # art final overrides to 2160
ap.add_argument("--audio",  help="master audio file")
ap.add_argument("--force",         action="store_true")
ap.add_argument("--allow-slates",  action="store_true")   # review only
ap.add_argument("--out",    type=Path, default=None)
ap.add_argument("--sheet", default="beat_sheet.json")

# Destination precedence for a clean master:
#   1. --out DIR       explicit, always wins
#   2. $ART_OUT        the downloader's configured render folder
#   3. <toolkit>/renders/   built-in default
# A --review cut is a working artifact and always stays beside the reel.
props.sparkLine: One script. --review vs. no --review = two verbs.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — final_preflight (paperwork triad + beat_lint + gate_shape). Verbatim from compile.py:454-466.
beats.narration_text: When --review is off, final_preflight runs before a single frame renders. It calls require_paperwork — a FACTCHECK, a SHOTLIST, and a PROMPTS file, each nonempty. Then it runs beat_lint and gate_shape as executable Python. If either gate exits non-zero, final refuses. The lint runs on the sheet, not the mp4 — you fail fast, before you spend the render.

beats.role_note: WORKED EXAMPLE — the happy path. Verbatim from demo/RUN-LOG.txt section 2.
beats.narration_text: Here is a tiny reel with one still, three seconds of narration, and the three paperwork files. Art final prints a single line per beat, a motion histogram, a build stamp, then the mp4 path. Next to the mp4 is a verified.json file the compiler wrote itself — the SHA-256 of the export, and the SHA-256 of every input that fed it. This receipt is what downstream tools use to match the file to its recipe.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — atomic candidate write pattern. Verbatim from compile.py:803-825.
beats.narration_text: The atomic bit. Compile.py encodes into a candidate.mp4 inside a temp folder next to your --out. Only after Gate V passes and the approvals recheck succeeds does the candidate get os.replaced onto the final path. If any check fails — Gate V, an approval turning stale mid-render, a source file changing hash — the temp folder is thrown away, the previous verified export stays in place, and build-state records the failure. There is never a moment when the file on disk is between two versions.

show.event: gate V + approvals recheck lines type

props.title: compile.py:803-825 — atomic replace
props.code:
# The last-good-file guarantee (verbatim, compile.py:803-825):
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(
        prefix=f'.{slug}-candidate-', dir=out_dir) as scratch:
    candidate = Path(scratch) / 'candidate.mp4'
    cmd[-1] = str(candidate)
    sh(cmd)                                    # encode into the temp
    verify_output(candidate, total, fps, …)    # decode + duration + audio
    if not a.review:
        gate = … 'runtime/qc/final_frame_check.py'
        timeline = work / 'resolved-sheet.json'
        atomic_json(timeline, sheet)           # resolved-clock sheet for Gate V
        sh([sys.executable, gate, folder,
            '--mp4',   candidate,
            '--sheet', timeline])              # Gate V on the candidate
        latest = json.loads((folder / a.sheet).read_text())
        validate_approvals(folder, latest)     # re-check approvals
        if latest != original_sheet:
            raise BuildError('Beat sheet changed during rendering…')
        if any(not Path(p).is_file() or file_digest(p) != value
               for p, value in input_hashes.items()):
            raise BuildError('Source media or narration changed…')
    os.replace(candidate, out)                 # the atomic swap
props.sparkLine: Encode into a temp. Replace only after every check clears.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — the receipt. Five keys, machine claim only; publication is a separate human step.
beats.narration_text: The receipt is five keys. Status equals ready. Output — the absolute path. SHA-256 of the mp4. Input_sha256 — every media file and every narration mp3 hashed by name. Duration_s from the timeline the audio built. And a timestamp. Ready is a machine claim about the checks that just passed. It is not human approval, and it is not a promise of YouTube 4K processing. Publication is a separate human step.

show.event: card in; title '<slug>.verified.json — the machine receipt'

props.title: <slug>.verified.json — the machine receipt
props.code:
# compile.py — the receipt writer (verbatim shape):
state = {
  'status':       'review' if a.review else 'ready',
  'output':       str(out.resolve()),
  'sha256':       file_digest(out),           # SHA-256 of the mp4 you just wrote
  'duration_s':   total,
  'input_sha256': input_hashes,               # {path: sha256} for every input
  'at':           datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
}
if not a.review:
    atomic_json(out.with_suffix('.verified.json'), state)
atomic_json(writable_path(folder, 'build-state.json'), state)

# Read side — downstream tooling matches file to recipe:
receipt = json.loads(Path(f'{out}.verified.json'.replace('.mp4', '')).read_text())
assert receipt['sha256'] == sha256_of(out), 'file drifted from its receipt'
# 'ready' says these automated checks passed — it does NOT mean:
#   * a human watched the film                (see FEEDBACK.md)
#   * YouTube 4K processing succeeded          (checked post-upload)
#   * professors approved publication          (out of scope for art)
props.sparkLine: Ready is a machine claim. Publication is a human step.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — empty FACTCHECK.md refuses, previous export preserved. Verbatim from demo/RUN-LOG.txt section 3.
beats.narration_text: One failure worth showing. Same reel. Truncate FACTCHECK.md to zero bytes — mimicking the accidental commit that empties a paperwork file. Re-run. Art final refuses immediately: gate F, missing or empty. The mp4 in exports is unchanged; the SHA-256 you had before is the SHA-256 you have now. The recovery is one line — put a real sentence back in FACTCHECK.md — and the next art final exits zero.

show.event: card in; title reads 'recovery   (verbatim; empty FACTCHECK)'
BEFORE: exports contain a ready mp4 + verified.json
AFTER: refused — GATE F: missing or empty FACTCHECK.md

props.title: recovery   (verbatim; empty FACTCHECK, previous mp4 untouched)
props.code:
# BEFORE — last successful export
$ shasum -a 256 /tmp/…/exports/art-final-demo.mp4
5910ade9793c943b2…3403eb5eecfae93e3  /tmp/…/exports/art-final-demo.mp4

# ---------------- EDIT ----------------
$ echo -n '' > /tmp/claude-501/art-final-demo/FACTCHECK.md

# AFTER — same reel, empty paperwork file
$ ./art final /tmp/claude-501/art-final-demo --out … --height 1080
[art] REFUSED: GATE F: missing or empty FACTCHECK.md;
  review is allowed, final is blocked
[exit 2]

# The last-good-file guarantee, observed:
$ shasum -a 256 /tmp/…/exports/art-final-demo.mp4
5910ade9793c943b2…3403eb5eecfae93e3  /tmp/…/exports/art-final-demo.mp4   ← same
$ cat /tmp/…/build-state.json
{ "status": "failed",
  "error":  "GATE F: missing or empty FACTCHECK.md…",
  "at":     "2026-09-09T…" }

# RECOVERY — put a real sentence back and re-run
$ echo 'One demonstration beat.' > /tmp/…/FACTCHECK.md
$ ./art final /tmp/claude-501/art-final-demo --out … --height 1080
[art] wrote /tmp/…/exports/art-final-demo.mp4  (3.0s, …)
[exit 0]
props.sparkLine: Refusal preserves the last good file. Recovery is one line.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — six-line recap of the whole surface, in the order you use it.
beats.narration_text: So — art final. One dispatcher branch, one Python script, two verbs. It gates the paperwork, encodes into a temp, gates the pixels, re-checks approvals, and only then swaps the file in. It writes a receipt beside the mp4. Slates and pending signatures block the master unconditionally. Every guarantee — last good file preserved, receipt matches file, sheet did not drift mid-render — falls out of that same atomic pattern.

show.event: heading types: 'art final — the whole surface, in the order you use it'

props.artifactHeading: art final — the whole surface, in the order you use it
artifactLines: bare invocation — ./art final <reel> [--out DIR] [--height 2160]; forwards to python3 runtime/scripts/compile.py.
one script, two verbs — --review writes a slate-marked cut beside the reel; no --review writes a clean master to --out.
final_preflight fails fast — paperwork triad + beat_lint + gate_shape run before the first ffmpeg call.
atomic candidate write — candidate encodes into a temp, gates run against it, os.replace swaps it in; a failure never overwrites the last verified export.
verified.json is the receipt — SHA-256 of the mp4, SHA-256 of every input, duration, ISO timestamp; ready is a machine claim, not human sign-off.
slates and approvals block the master — --allow-slates is review-only, --no-gate cannot bypass approvals; a pending signature never ships.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer. Prompt read aloud verbatim, then discussed.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code, pointed at a reel folder you finished this week. Run art final with a --out flag pointed at a fresh directory. Copy the printed SHA-256 out of exports and hash the file yourself with shasum minus a two-five-six. If those two strings match, the receipt describes the file. If they do not, something wrote to your export after the compile — investigate before you share the video.

props.segment: Verify your export against its receipt
props.command: From the brutalist.art toolkit root against a reel I finished this week: (1) ./art final <reel> --out /tmp/verify-<reel> --height 2160. (2) cat the sibling <slug>.verified.json and copy the sha256. (3) Independently hash the mp4 with shasum -a 256. (4) Report whether the two strings match character-for-character; if not, list every file modified in the export directory in the last minute.
output: expect verified.json.sha256 == shasum -a 256 of the mp4
if they diverge, the receipt is stale; investigate before sharing
